presentation.caption: White has picked a move, which Black does not see before playing theirs.
presentation.intro: No more advantage for White: each turn, both players pick a move without knowing their opponent's, then the two moves are revealed and played together.

points.intermediateTurn: A piece venturing onto an attacked square can be captured in an intermediate turn.
points.kingCapture: A king can be captured outright, even without checkmate.
points.sameSquare: Two pieces heading for the same square capture each other, and two pieces can swap places.

presentation.rooms: Create a room, private with a password, or join one of the open rooms. Each participant picks a color; the others watch the game.
presentation.tagline: Chess where both players move at the same time.
presentation.title: Synchronous chess

capture.text: … a piece moves to a square held by an opposing piece that did not move this turn, that piece is captured. The piece that moved takes the freed square.
capture.title: Capture

clash.text: … both pieces move to the same square, they are both captured and removed from the board, a king included.
clash.title: Clash

swap.text: … a piece moves to a square held before the turn by an opposing piece that moved as well, both pieces reach their destination without being captured, even if their paths cross.
swap.title: Swap

end.caption: Ends of the game and their result
end.fiftyTurns: 50 synchronous turns without a pawn move or a capture
end.insufficientMaterial: Not enough pieces to checkmate: kings alone, a single knight or bishop, bishops all on squares of the same color
end.kingCaptured: King captured, by moving to the same square as an opposing piece
end.opponentUnlessBothKings: for the opponent (a draw if both kings are captured)
end.stalemate: Stalemate: a player who is not in check cannot move any piece
end.text: A captured king ends the game at once. Otherwise, the game ends at the start of a synchronous turn.
end.threefoldRepetition: The same position (pieces and castling rights) occurs for the third time
end.title: End of the game

inShort.endOfGame: End of the game: checkmate or a captured king; the draws of classic chess apply.
inShort.intermediateTurns: Intermediate turns: a piece arriving on an attacked square can be captured right away.
inShort.sameSquare: Same square: two pieces moving to the same square are both captured, a king included.
inShort.simultaneousMoves: Simultaneous moves: each player picks a move in secret, then both moves are played together.
inShort.title: In short

intermediate.backToGame: Back to the game. The game then resumes with a synchronous turn.
intermediate.captures: Captures and recaptures. The opponent can capture this piece, or pass. Only the captures on the squares concerned are allowed; each capture can in turn be recaptured, until a player can no longer, or no longer wants to, capture. If both players may play, their moves are chosen in secret and applied simultaneously.
intermediate.oncePerPiece: Once per piece. A piece can move only once during the intermediate phase. The piece that just moved during the synchronous turn can still move once in it.
intermediate.title: Intermediate turns
intermediate.trigger: Trigger. After a synchronous turn, an intermediate turn takes place if a piece that moved arrived on a square already attacked (or protected) by the opponent before the turn, and an opposing piece can legally capture it.

players.seats: Two players. Each participant of the room, the host included, picks a color among the free seats. The seats are set from the first move played; the other participants are spectators. Until then, the other player or the host may free the seat of a player away.
players.simultaneousMoves: Both players play their move simultaneously, each without knowing the other's move. Once both players have chosen, the two moves are revealed and applied according to the rules below.
players.title: Players and principle

promotion.text: If at least one player brings a pawn to the last rank, a dedicated turn lets them choose its promotion. The game then resumes with the synchronous or intermediate turn resulting from the moves played.
promotion.title: Promotion

restrictions.castling: Castling: a king in check cannot castle out of it. Check prevents castling for this turn only; the right to castle is lost only once the king or the rook has moved.
restrictions.check: Check: a king attacked at the start of the synchronous turn must move to a square that is not attacked before the moves. If it cannot, it is checkmate.
restrictions.kingSquares: Squares forbidden to the king: it cannot go to a square attacked by the opponent before the synchronous turn; there is no point anticipating that a square will be freed to move there.
restrictions.pinnedPieces: Pinned pieces: no move can leave one's own king attacked, the opponent's position being assumed unchanged; a pinned piece cannot leave the line of its king.
restrictions.title: Restrictions
